hypothesis: When the policy rate sits more than 1 point above a simple Taylor rule (tight), the central bank cuts within 6 months more often than in any month; when it sits more than 1 point below (loose), it hikes within 6 months more often than in any month.
knownLimits: No output gap: the IMF estimate is annual and revised each vintage, so the rule here is rate = 2% + inflation + 0.5 x (inflation - target).
Inflation is today's OECD vintage, lagged 2 months to roughly what was published; revisions are not undone.
The dated target table (src/data/inflationTargetHistory.ts) is part of this test; a country is tested only in months with a confirmed published target.
Turkey, pegged currencies and banks without a numeric target are left out.
Years of rates near zero make 'loose' readings common and long; only the first month of each run counts as a call.
Cases are treated as independent in the p-value; calls in one country are separated by at least one month with a different reading.
